body: 4.   [News • 6 hours ago A third straight robust jobs report just laid the groundwork for a potential Fed rate hike later this year](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/strong-may-jobs-report-will-keep-fed-focused-on-inflation-with-possibility-of-hikes-later-this-year-134835143.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [Stocks fell on Wednesday](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-losses-accelerate-after-fed-decision-as-powell-touts-inflation-worries-185152647.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead)and [Thursday](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-recover-from-steep-losses-as-oils-surge-eases-200040220.html) after Fed Chair Jerome Powell underscored the uncertainty surrounding the oil shock during his press conference and said the US had not made as much progress on inflation as it had hoped. > In comments to reporters on Wednesday, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell acknowledged that the oil crisis resulting from the Iran war [could drive up inflation](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/federal-reserve-holds-interest-rates-steady-keeps-1-cut-in-play-this-year-as-uncertainty-mounts-130010108.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead). > Even as he said “there will be some effects on inflation going forward," the Fed chair stuck to the same line when asked to make predictions about just how large the effects of the war in the Middle East could be: "The implications of [developments in the Middle East](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-futures-fall-oil-surges-after-iran-inflation-worries-sink-stocks-225027246.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead) on the US economy are uncertain.". [_Read more here._](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/what-fed-chair-jerome-powell-said--and-didnt-say--about-the-oil-crisis-100021823.html). [_Read more about the day's market moves in stocks, bonds, oil, and more._](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-losses-accelerate-after-fed-decision-as-powell-touts-inflation-worries-185152647.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead).

While the [Middle East conflict](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/global-research/current-events/iran-conflict-ripple-effects) has sent energy prices soaring, the Federal Reserve (Fed) opted to keep interest rates steady at 3.5–3.75% at its last meeting in March. Generally, the Fed is seen as more likely to cut rates only if the [labor market](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/global-research/outlook/labor-market-forecast-2026) weakens significantly or if the economic fallout from higher energy prices becomes more severe. In what may have been Chair [Jerome Powell](https://www.cnbc.com/jay-powell/)’s final meeting at the helm, the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee voted to hold the benchmark funds rate in a range between 3.5%-3.75%. Separately, during a news conference following the central bank’s decision, Powell signaled that he would [remain on the Board of Governors for an indefinite period](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/jerome-powell-says-he-will-continue-to-serve-as-a-fed-governor-even-after-chairmanship-ends-.html). ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/fed-interest-rate-decision-april-2026.html)‘Inflation is elevated’. Markets had been widely expecting the hold and in fact are [pricing in no changes the rest of this year](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/28/fed-meeting-preview-april-2026.html) and well into 2027. Fed officials at the [March meeting](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/18/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html) indicated they foresee one cut this year then another in 2027, putting the funds rate down to its expected “neutral” level around 3.1%. ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/fed-interest-rate-decision-april-2026.html)Powell’s choice.
